title: narration/2 — ordered narration segments; speech carries its verbatim quote as its own field, separate from staging prose
description: Supersedes narration/1, which folded a spoken line and the staging around it into one `text` string. That forced every consumer to guess where the quote began: the frontend could not style speech differently from prose, and the verbatim belt had to substring-match a whole sentence of narrator writing against a perception line. Splitting them makes the spoken words a first-class field — the UI formats them, and the belt checks exactly the words claimed to be spoken and nothing else.

speaker_id.description: The PRESENT id this segment is attributed to; null for narrator prose. Never the viewer: he is not in PRESENT and his own words and acts are narration.

kind.description: narration = the narrator's own voice (scene, atmosphere, outcomes, anything not one person's clean act). action = one NPC's clean single act. speech = one NPC saying words.

text.description: Prose. For narration and action it is the whole segment and must be non-empty. For speech it is the STAGING around the line ("she leans in, her voice dropping") and MAY be empty when the line is delivered bare — the words themselves never live here.

quote.description: The verbatim spoken words, WITHOUT quotation marks and without any attribution or staging. Non-empty exactly when kind is speech; null otherwise. This is the field the verbatim belt checks against what the speaker was perceived to say.
